title: Troubleshooting Common PHP Problems
learning_outcomes: Explain what troubleshooting common php problems contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: incorrect file paths.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. In this lesson, focus on incorrect file paths; then compare it with missing extensions. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use troubleshooting common php problems when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. For troubleshooting common php problems, begin with incorrect file paths. Also distinguish missing extensions; namespace and autoloading errors; incorrect types and array keys. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Incorrect file paths
items.text: Check the operation result, use a known storage boundary, and consider empty files, permissions, invalid paths, and cleanup.

items.title: Missing extensions
items.text: Know when to use missing extensions, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Namespace and autoloading errors
items.text: Keep package metadata and source layout consistent, and verify version constraints and class-to-file mapping with the selected tools.

items.title: Incorrect types and array keys
items.text: Trace the input keys and values, then verify the resulting order and shape, including empty collections and missing keys.

items.title: Permission and configuration issues
items.text: Distinguish identity verification from resource permission, and test expiry, invalid credentials, and denied access as well as the success path.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Troubleshooting Common PHP Problems
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet as example.php. Run `php -l example.php` to check syntax, then run `php example.php` locally when the example has no external-service or framework prerequisites. Some examples are syntax-only illustrations and require the noted extension or framework to run meaningfully.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for troubleshooting common php problems from top to bottom. Start by identifying incorrect file paths, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for troubleshooting common php problems that demonstrates "incorrect file paths". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of incorrect file paths.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Troubleshooting Common PHP Problems is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.
